purpose: Record the ACTUAL git line-ending behaviour of the R74 PHASE B1 committed files, and correct an earlier apples-to-oranges hash comparison.
earlier_error: A first metadata attempt compared Get-FileHash SHA-256 of the work bytes against `git hash-object --stdin` / `git rev-parse` output. `git hash-object` and `git rev-parse HEAD:path` return a SHA-1 git OBJECT name, not a SHA-256 of the bytes, so a SHA-256!=SHA-1 mismatch is NOT evidence of CRLF/LF normalization. That comparison is discarded.
correct_method: SHA-256 of the work-file bytes vs SHA-256 of the actual blob bytes (git cat-file blob HEAD:path), plus git check-attr text/eol.

gitattributes_in_effect.repo_level: * text=auto ; *.py/*.md/*.txt/*.json/*.yaml/*.yml text eol=lf ; *.ps1 text eol=crlf ; core.autocrlf=true
gitattributes_in_effect.round74_dir_level: runs/.../round74_constrained_early_head_adaptation/.gitattributes = `* -text` (deeper file wins for the text attribute)
gitattributes_in_effect.check_attr_result: text: unset ; eol: lf  (the deeper `* -text` unsets text, so NO end-of-line normalization is applied to these files)

conclusion: All four R74 PHASE B1 files are stored BYTE-IDENTICAL to their work bytes (LF preserved, work_CRLF=0, blob_CRLF=0). The round74-dir `* -text` disables normalization, so the earlier 'DIFFERENT' reading was purely the SHA-256-vs-SHA-1 algorithm mix-up. No original receipt is rewritten; this record is additive.
scope_note: Only the NEW PHASE B1 files are re-hashed here. Pre-existing PHASE A receipts are left byte-identical and are not re-tested for formatting.
